(6) AFTER photos once controls are in place to document the improvement. (7) Close the loop: when rotator is back up, verify scrap backlog is cleared and normal flow is restored. knowledge.subject: Copper kit cart push/pull ergo limit â Snook women's 75th, pull governs at 521 lbs product
knowledge.detail: Push/pull force study on copper kit carts (Jad Samaha) vs Snook tables, women's 75th-percentile basis: init pull/push limit 44 lbf; sust push 24.25; sust pull 26.46. Weights are product-only (cart excluded). Initial PULL governs (hardest task). Regression: pull force = 0.0464*(product lbs) + 19.82, R^2=0.988 -> 44 lbf at 521 lbs product. 521 = 50/50 line (mean=44; ~half of pulls exceed; over-pulls run ~47-51 lbf). knowledge.subject: LESSON: Bash heredoc dollar-sign corruption in JSON POSTs
knowledge.detail: WORKFLOW LESSON. When POSTing JSON via curl with bash heredoc using unquoted delimiter (<<JSON), embedded dollar signs (e.g. $5K, $400K) get variable-substituted to empty strings before the request is sent. Knowledge entry K5 (DC guns) lost its dollar signs on first push ("$5K each" became "K each"), required DELETE + re-POST to fix. Prevention: use single-quoted heredoc (<<'JSON') when JSON contains literal $, or use -d '{...}' with single-quoted inline JSON. knowledge.subject: Snook & Ciriello tables for push/pull cart safety
knowledge.detail: Cart push/pull safety uses Snook & Ciriello psychophysical tables (Liberty Mutual Research Institute), not NIOSH equation. Tables are empirical lookup â cross-reference gender, push vs pull, initial vs sustained force, handle height, distance, and frequency to get Maximum Acceptable Force (MAF) at population percentile thresholds (75%, 90%, etc.). Target: 90% threshold = 35 lb initial force for males. Current 700 lb cart data shows 45-46 lb start force, exceeding safe threshold. Variables affecting force: cart weight, wheel size, wheel material, floor condition, distance, handle height, frequency. Larger wheels = less force. Better floor = less force. Frequency increase can offset weight reduction but may create new hazards.
